Figure 1.PBR texture gallery generated by UltraTex.Our method produces detailed and physically plausible PBR materials across diverse assets under environmental lighting.
In the first row, the right column shows the generated albedo, metallic, and roughness maps from top to bottom.
In the second row, a close-up render (right) of the boxed region (left) reveals fine-grained material details.
Project page:https://ultratex.vercel.app/.

Figure 2.Overall pipeline of UltraTex.UltraTex adopts a cascaded two-stage multi-view diffusion pipeline.
Stage 1 jointly predicts albedo maps and world-space shading normals from the reference image and multi-view geometry normals.
Stage 2 predicts metallic-roughness (MR) maps (where purple and green represent roughness and metallic, respectively) conditioned on the generated albedo, reference-image features, and VLM-derived intrinsic material tokens.
For MR training, photometric representation alignment uses a frozen visual encoder to extract representations from controlled-light material renderings, and an MLP aligns intermediate diffusion features to this photometric representation space viaℒREPA\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{REPA}}.

Figure 3.VLM-guided intrinsic material adapter.A frozen VLM extracts hidden-layer visual features from rendered reference images, and a trainable adapter projects them into 1D intrinsic material tokens.
With the image diffusion model frozen, the adapter is trained to reconstruct ground-truth metallic and roughness maps by injecting these tokens into the denoising blocks.
The learned tokens encode part-aware material semantic priors and are used to guide MR generation.

Figure 4.Effectiveness of joint albedo and shading-normal estimation.(a) Tangent-space normal or bump maps depend on local UV parameterization; continuous 3D surfaces may be unwrapped into disjoint UV patches with different orientations, leading to inconsistent tangent frames.
(b) By jointly estimating world-space shading normals with albedo, our model avoids such UV-dependent artifacts and produces richer surface details.
We compare against a model trained without joint shading-normal estimation, where the normal visualization corresponds to the input geometry normals.

Figure 6.Comparison with open source methods. Our method effectively eliminates baked-in lighting and shadows, ensuring the generation of physically accurate material attributes.
We show the albedo channel (left) alongside the metallic (top right) and roughness (bottom right) channels.

We show the albedo channel (left) alongside the metallic (top right) and roughness (bottom right) channels.

Figure 7.Comparison with SoTA commercial methods.Recent commercial methods often struggle with accurate metallic and roughness estimation. By integrating VLM-based physical reasoning and photometric consistency, UltraTex generates more accurate material attributes and richer material details. For each asset, we show the albedo channel (left) alongside the metallic (top right) and roughness (bottom right) channels.

Figure 8.Comparison of local details.Our model excels in generating ultra-fine albedo details with high fidelity, even for challenging surfaces such as oxidized metals and those characterized by intricate micro-textures.

Figure 9.Relighting Results.Our generated PBR textures exhibit physically plausible and consistent material responses under novel illumination conditions, faithfully reflecting changes in highlights and reflections.

Figure 10.Results on real-world captures.Our method produces accurate and physically plausible PBR textures from casually captured images and scanned meshes, demonstrating robustness to real-world inputs.

Figure 11.Qualitative comparison with ground-truth PBR maps. Given the same clay mesh and reference image, our method more faithfully recovers the ground-truth material decomposition than the state-of-the-art multi-view and 3D-native baselines, with finer base-color details, cleaner metallic separation, and more accurate spatially varying roughness. Each object has: the albedo on the left, the metallic on the top right, and the roughness on the bottom right.

Figure 12.Impact of semantic and photometric alignment. The first row visualizes our VLM adapter capturing intrinsic material semantics. The following rows compare metallic and roughness maps of ablated variants and our full model. Without VLM-derived tokens, the network incorrectly predicts non-metallic surfaces (e.g., painted fish, plastic TV casing) as metallic. Removing photometric alignment yields weaker metallic contrast and fails to recover structural details like gears, rivets, and screws.

Figure 13.VLM-token attention visualization. We visualize the attention map from VLM material tokens to noisy image tokens. The attention maps exhibit clear spatial localization over material-relevant object parts, such as metallic ornaments and hardware, indicating that the 1D material tokens capture part-aware material correspondence.

Figure 14.Multi-view input pipeline. Our framework naturally extends to multi-view references by independently encoding each input view and pairing its image features with the corresponding geometry tokens in the Multi-Modal DiT, while leaving the remaining generation pipeline unchanged.

Figure 15.Normal map transformation. Our predicted shading normals are converted to a tangent-space normal map, adding fine-scale surface details to the original clay mesh without modifying its geometry.

Figure 16.Failure Cases. Highly stylized assets may use MR for artistic rather than physical effects, leading to ambiguous decomposition, as seen in the joker’s hair and the character’s garments. In addition, effects beyond the opaque metallic–roughness model, such as the vehicle’s transparent windshield, cannot be faithfully represented.
Figure 17.More Qualitative Results.We present additional PBR comparisons with other methods (from left to right: albedo, metallic, roughness). Zooming in for details.
Figure 18.More results.We provide additional multi-view renderings with their corresponding generated PBR maps. Zooming in is recommended to observe the ultra-fine albedo and material details.
